title: Explicit finite basis affine dual comparisons commute with precomposition
statement: Let Y be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], U an affine open, A=Γ(Y,U), and T the associated sheaf functor followed by transport along U.isoSpec. Let M,N be A-modules with specified finite bases bM indexed by I and bN indexed by J. Define eM:Hom(T(M),O_U) ≅ T(Hom_A(M,A)) by transporting M to the free sheaf using bM, using the canonical internal dual of the free sheaf, and transporting the dual-basis representation back to the associated sheaf of the module dual; define eN similarly. For every A-linear map f:N→M, precomposition by T(f) followed by eN equals eM followed by T(precomposition by f). Bases may have different index sets, including empty sets; A may be the zero ring. The data of both isomorphisms are constructed from the specified bases and closed library constructions, independently of the theorem.

proof.text: Use Tag 01HV(4)-(5) to identify sections on a principal open with localizations and all restrictions with localization maps. The explicit tildeFinsupp and restrictFreeIso comparisons carry the given basis vectors to the localized free generators. The canonical homObjFreeUnitIso records evaluation on those generators. Basis.dualBasis_repr identifies the module dual coordinates with the same evaluations.

Write f in the two finite bases with matrix (a_ij). Both composites in the naturality equation send the evaluation vector (v_i) to (sum_i a_ij v_i)_j. This is a finite sum; localization preserves it. Thus the two maps agree on each principal open, including empty bases and the zero ring.

The principal opens are a basis. Apply the sheaf property to equality on this basis, and transport the equality along U.isoSpec. No assertion about complexes or their differential signs occurs in this lemma.

lean.statement:
theorem affineBasisDualIso_naturality {Y : Scheme.{u}} (U : Y.affineOpens)
    (M N : ModuleCat.{u} Γ(Y, U.1)) {I J : Type u} [Fintype I] [Fintype J]
    (bM : Basis I Γ(Y, U.1) M) (bN : Basis J Γ(Y, U.1) N) (f : N ⟶ M) :
    let T := tilde.functor Γ(Y, U.1) ⋙ Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor U.2.isoSpec.hom
    SheafOfModules.homObjMap (R := U.1.toScheme.toRingedSpace.sheaf)
        (T.map f) (𝟙 (SheafOfModules.unit U.1.toScheme.ringCatSheaf)) ≫
      (affineBasisDualIso U N bN).hom =
    (affineBasisDualIso U M bM).hom ≫
      T.map (ModuleCat.ofHom (Linear.leftComp Γ(Y, U.1)
        (ModuleCat.of Γ(Y, U.1) Γ(Y, U.1)) f))
